original.target_description: Study 1: testosterone, high- versus low-power posing; Time-2 hormone ANCOVA controlling baseline and other hormone, with sex controlled in testosterone analyses

n.location: p. 1364 (PDF p. 2), Participants; p. 1366 (PDF p. 4), hormone analysis; p. 1368 (PDF p. 6), Note 2
n.quote: Forty-two participants (26 females and 16 males) ... Analyses with cortisol controlled for testosterone, and vice versa. ... two outliers that were more than 3 standard deviations above the mean and were excluded; testosterone scores ... one outlier that was more than 3 standard deviations above the mean and was excluded.
n.sample_role: participants in baseline-adjusted hormone ANCOVA; analytic n not explicitly printed
n.exclusions: Two cortisol outliers and one testosterone outlier excluded; overlap and handling of missing covariate values not specified, so analytic n for the mutually adjusted tests cannot be securely established.

replication.target_description: Study 1: testosterone, high- versus low-power posing; independent two-tailed t test of Time-2 minus Time-1 changes

n.location: p. 653 (PDF p. 1), Method; p. 656 (PDF p. 4), Note 3; p. 654 (PDF p. 2), Results
n.quote: Of the final sample of 200, 98 were women and 102 men. ... Hormonal levels were not detectable in one saliva sample. An additional sample was lost during the storage and transportation process. ... t(196)
n.sample_role: participants with hormonal data; 198 established from final 200 minus 2 missing, consistent with t-test df
n.exclusions: One sample with undetectable hormone levels; one additional sample lost during storage/transport.

reported_success.quote: we failed to confirm an effect of power posing on testosterone, cortisol, and financial risk taking.

notes: Original locator p.5 points to figures/additional-study discussion in the published PDF; matching main-study tests are on PDF p.4 (journal p.1366). Additional N=49 study on PDF p.5 was not substituted. Original analytic n is left null because mutually adjusted hormone analyses and unspecified outlier overlap prevent secure test-specific n. Replication analytic n is established from explicitly reported total and missing counts, corroborated by t-test df; the resulting analytic count is not separately printed.
